name: Consumer 3D Printing
thesis_at_peak: Additive manufacturing would move production into the home and every household would print replacement parts on demand.
what_happened: The technology worked and continued to improve. It simply turned out to be a tool for prototyping and low-volume specialist parts rather than a general substrate for making things. Industrial adoption grew steadily and profitably while the consumer thesis, which was the part that justified the multiples, never arrived.
lesson: A working technology with a real cost curve can still fail as a theme if it is a tool rather than a substrate. Ask what fraction of the addressable use cases it serves better than the incumbent method — for additive it was small, and it stayed small.

name: Blockchain As Enterprise Infrastructure
thesis_at_peak: Distributed ledgers would replace enterprise databases, supply chain records, land registries and settlement systems.
what_happened: There was no threshold to cross. Every proposed enterprise application was already served by a database that was faster, cheaper and administratively simpler. The technology solved trustlessness, which is expensive, in settings where the participants already trusted each other. A decade of pilots produced almost no production systems.
lesson: Verify that the problem being solved is one someone actually has. A capability with no unmet need behind it generates pilots indefinitely and revenue never. This is distinct from a technology that is early: fifteen years is not early.

name: Consumer Virtual Reality
thesis_at_peak: Immersive computing would become the successor interface to the smartphone.
what_happened: Hardware improved on every measurable axis — resolution, weight, latency, price — and adoption still stalled. The obstacle was never the specification. It was that people decline to wear a device on their face, and no amount of curve improvement addresses that.
lesson: This is the single most useful entry in the file. It is the case where the cost and capability curves both behaved and the theme still failed, because the unlock required a behaviour change people would not make. Run the return test — did a real person come back to it unprompted a week later — before believing any capability curve.

name: Graphene
thesis_at_peak: A material with extraordinary properties would displace silicon, transform batteries, and create a new materials industry.
what_happened: Laboratory properties never survived scale manufacture. Producing graphene with consistent quality in volume stayed expensive and the cost curve essentially flattened. The Nobel Prize was awarded for the science, which was real; the industry did not follow.
lesson: A property demonstrated in a laboratory is not a cost curve. Require evidence that the curve exists at manufacturing scale, over several years, before treating a material as a theme.

name: Hydrogen Passenger Vehicles
thesis_at_peak: Fuel cells would power passenger cars and hydrogen would replace petrol in the light vehicle fleet.
what_happened: The competing curve fell faster. Lithium-ion pack prices dropped roughly sixteen percent annually for over a decade while green hydrogen costs stayed roughly flat, and the round-trip efficiency gap never closed. Hydrogen retains a defensible case in steel, shipping, fertiliser and long-haul freight — the failure was specific to passenger cars.
lesson: Never assess a cost curve in isolation. It competes against another curve, and the relevant question is the gap between them and its direction. A curve that falls while a rival falls faster is a losing position that looks like progress on its own chart.

name: Nanotechnology
thesis_at_peak: Molecular manufacturing would allow atomically precise assembly and remake the entire industrial base.
what_happened: The general-purpose assembler was never built and is still not close. The funded research produced real and valuable results in coatings, semiconductors and materials science, all of which were absorbed into existing industries rather than forming a theme. Nothing was investable as nanotechnology.
lesson: When a theme's payoff depends on a capability that does not yet exist even in prototype, it is a research programme rather than an investment theme. The useful distinction is whether the exponential is already running and merely unnoticed, or has not started.
